summary.text: The atomic nucleus is the small, dense region of protons and neutrons at the center of an atom.
Almost all of an atom's mass is in the nucleus, and the nuclear force binds its protons and neutrons together.
Rutherford found it in 1911 when alpha particles deflected at large angles, which showed the plum pudding model could not be accurate.

facts.label: Diameter range
facts.value: About 1.70 fm for hydrogen to 11.7 fm for uranium

facts.label: Compared with atom
facts.value: The atom is about 27,000 to 60,000 times wider

facts.label: Possible shapes
facts.value: Spherical, rugby-ball, discus, triaxial or pear-shaped

items.prompt: If Thomson's plum pudding model had been right, what would Rutherford have expected from alpha particles fired at thin metal foil?

options.label: They would bounce straight back
They would pass through with very little deviation
They would be absorbed and vanish
They would turn into electrons

items.explain: Rutherford reasoned the positively charged alpha particles would easily pass through with very little deviation.

items.prompt: Many alpha particles bounced off a foil at very large angles. What did this tell Rutherford about the atom?

options.label: Its mass and positive charge sit in a dense center
Its charges are evenly spread out
Its electrons are packed into a solid shell
Its mass is carried only by the electrons

items.explain: The deflections could only be explained if the atom's mass was a concentrated point of positive charge.

items.prompt: What is the main job of neutrons inside a nucleus?

options.label: To attract the electrons toward the center
To give the nucleus its positive charge
To reduce the electrostatic repulsion in the nucleus
To pull the protons apart from one another

items.explain: The main role of neutrons is to reduce electrostatic repulsion inside the nucleus.

items.prompt: Two nuclei hold the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. What do they share?

options.label: The same mass, with a different identity
Both the same identity and the same mass
Neither identity nor mass in common
The same chemical identity, with a different mass

items.explain: Protons define the nucleus's charge and chemical identity, while neutrons add mass and explain isotopes.

items.prompt: The strong force binds protons and neutrons in a nucleus. What happens to it just beyond the nucleus's edge?

options.label: It drops essentially to zero
It grows stronger with distance
It stays the same as inside
It switches to pushing outward

items.explain: The nuclear strong force has a very short range and essentially drops to zero just beyond the edge of the nucleus.

items.prompt: What produces the chemistry we see in the everyday world?

options.label: Nuclei fusing together whenever two atoms touch
Atoms sharing electrons in stable orbits about their nuclei
Protons moving back and forth between nearby atoms
Neutrons attaching one atom firmly to another atom

items.explain: Sharing electrons to create stable electronic orbits about the nuclei appears to us as chemistry.
